description:
## Why

Without quotas a single user can fill the block store and degrade or crash the service for all users. Per-user quotas are required for a multi-tenant deployment.

## What

- users.quota_bytes column (NULL = unlimited) set at provisioning time
- Quota checked at two enforcement points:
  1. JMAP Email/set create and Email/import: reject with overQuota error if accepting the message would exceed the user's quota
  2. SMTP RCPT TO / DATA: return 452 4.2.2 (mailbox full) if the user is over quota
- Quota accounting: sum of byte_size for all messages belonging to the user (tracked in the messages metadata table, not the block store — shared blocks are counted per-user based on their logical ownership)
- JMAP Quota/get (RFC 9425) endpoint to let clients report quota status to users
- Admin CLI: stoa-mail user set-quota <username> <gb>

## Acceptance

- Users at or over quota cannot receive new mail via SMTP or JMAP
- overQuota JMAP error returned for Email/set create when over quota
- 452 returned by SMTP when recipient is over quota
- quota_bytes = NULL means unlimited (no enforcement)
- JMAP Quota/get returns current usage and limit for the authenticated user
notes: Block store dedup means two users receiving the same email share one block. Quota accounting is logical (per-user metadata byte count) not physical (block store bytes). This is correct: each user is charged for the mail they own regardless of dedup savings.
title: Per-user quota enforcement
